Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Body, health & movement

masseur noun

also masseuse, massage therapist

classical

Plin. Ep. 10.5.1

1iātralīptēs: long ī in -līpt- and a long final e (Lewis & Short leaves both unmarked). Greek ἰᾱτραλείπτης.

iātralīptēs1, iātralīptae m.

noun, first declension

massage therapist, a doctor who treats with oil and rubbing

Pliny asked Trajan for citizenship for his own.

Examples

  • gravissimā valētūdine ūsque ad perīculum vītae vexātus iātralīptēn assūmpsī

    when a very serious illness put my life in danger, I took on a massage therapistPlin. Ep. 10.5.1

Other words

  • tractātor, tractātōris m. — masseur

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 66.53

    Both passages cited for this and tractātrīx are scornful; M-O s.v. masseur gives fricātor and, with a query, tractātor.

  • tractātrīx, tractātrīcis f. — masseuse

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Mart. 3.82.13

  • fricātor

    also used · post-classical · M-O s.v. masseur

  • 2alīptēs: long ī (Lewis & Short ăliptēs, leaving the i unmarked). Greek ἀλείπτης.

    alīptēs2, alīptae m. — the trainer who oiled and rubbed down athletes

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 1.9.15

  • 3ūnctor: long u before -nct- (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). A hidden quantity: the vowel before -nct- is long. Ruling: Macrons are spelling.

    ūnctor3, ūnctōris m. — anointer

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic.; Mart.

See also massage, rub with oil.
